question: to the Commission Regina Doherty (PPE) Subject:

The Commission has presented the next iteration of Horizon Europe, called Framework Programme 10 for Research and Innovation (FP10), to Parliament and the Council as part of the legislative process1. It said that the European Competitiveness Fund (ECF) would be ‘tightly linked to FP10’, for which EUR 175 billion was earmarked. The ECF has four policy ‘windows’, with funding for FP10 coming from pillars three and four. However, Article 182 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) may prohibit the ECF from being used to fund FP10. This issue was aired during the summer of 2025 and means that the Commission cannot now finance FP10 through the ECF. If so, this places the Commission in a serious predicament. University associations apparently expected a legal opinion and/or comment to be given during the Danish Presidency, but as yet the Commission has not issued a statement. 1.
What is the legal opinion from the Commission on whether Article 182 of TFEU prohibits the ECF from funding FP10?
If it is prohibited, how will the Commission finance FP10?

Mario Draghi had suggested that the ECF should have four policy ‘windows’. What happened to this plan? In particular, what happened to the funding that had been allocated for policies 3 and 4, which had been intended for research and innovation?
COM(2025)0543.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (2.6.2026) The proposal for the European Competitiveness Fund1 (ECF) and the proposed Framework Programme for research2 (FP10) will have closely coordinated programming of activities. In particular, certain actions under FP10 (those collaborative research actions under the ‘Competitiveness’ part of the FP10 Pillar II falling in a policy area also covered by an ECF policy window) will be programmed in specific dedicated parts of single work programmes. Moreover, the specific programme on defence research is integrated with the policy window covering defence as part of the ECF proposal (thus also mirroring the current setup of the European Defence Fund3 in that window). However, there is no legal issue as regards funding of the programmes as both ECF and FP10 have separate budgetary envelopes; ECF actions will be financed from ECF budget and FP10 actions will be financed from FP10 budget. Where an action contributes to objectives of both the ECF and FP10, it could be financed from both envelopes taking the form of, for example, a synergy call. The architecture proposed by the Commission for the ECF indeed foresees four policy windows. To ensure a seamless investment journey – from research to manufacturing and market deployment – the Commission has proposed to mirror the same policy windows within Pillar II of Horizon Europe (2028- 2034)4, under its ‘Competitiveness’ component. Horizon Europe will fund the research and innovation activities of the policy windows, while the ECF will focus on later stages of the investment journey, including scale-up manufacturing and market deployment. A tight connection between the two programmes will be ensured through single work programmes, in line with the proposed regulations.
1 https://commission.europa.eu/publications/european-competitiveness-fund_en. 2 See the proposal for Horizon Europe 2028-2034 - https://commission.europa.eu/publications/horizon-
